en: In the autumn of the following year, Nobuko accompanied her husband on his business trip to Tokyo, and together they returned to the hometown she had been away from for so long.
u.src: 第二年的秋天，信子陪出差东京的丈夫，一起回到了阔别已久的故乡。

en: Her husband had a great deal of work to finish during the brief business trip, so after hurriedly taking Nobuko to see his mother, he had no more time to go out with her.
u.src: 丈夫要在短暂的出差期间完成很多工作，因此只匆忙带着信子看望了一下母亲，就再也没时间陪她外出。

en: When Nobuko went to the suburbs to visit her younger sister Teruko, she also went alone, taking the train to the terminal stop, New Development District Station, and then continuing by rickshaw.
u.src: 信子去郊外看望妹妹照子的时候，也是一个人乘车到电车终点站新开发区站，然后坐人力车去的。

en: Teruko's newlywed home stood where the town met the green onion fields, in an area crowded with newly built rental houses.
u.src: 照子的新婚房屋在城镇和大葱地的交接地带，那附近以新建的出租房为主，房子盖得很是密集。

en: Every house was built in much the same way, with no real difference even in the eaved gates, the photinia hedges, or the bamboo poles for drying laundry.
u.src: 每家每户的构造都差不多，包括带檐的大门，光叶石楠篱笆，甚至晾晒衣服的竹竿都没什么差别。

en: Because the new house was so ordinary, Nobuko felt a little disappointed.
u.src: 新房子这么普通，信子心里有点失望。

en: But when she knocked at the door, the person who came to open it was, unexpectedly, her cousin.
u.src: 但是，等她敲门的时候，来开门的竟然是表兄。

en: Seeing Nobuko again after so long, Shunkichi happily called out, "Hey!" just as he always had,
u.src: 看到久违的信子，俊吉如以往一般开心的叫“呀——”，

en: and only then did Nobuko notice that Shunkichi no longer had the close-cropped hair he used to have.
u.src: 信子这才注意到，俊吉不再是从前一般的寸头了。

en: "It really has been a long time."
u.src: “真的好久不见呢。”

en: "Please, come in. Unfortunately, Teruko is not home; I am the only one here right now."
u.src: “快点请进来，不过十分不巧，照子不在家，现在只有我自己。”
“照子去哪了？”

en: "She went out on an errand with the maid."
u.src: “她和女佣一起出去办事了。”

en: Nobuko felt an inexplicable sense of shame,
u.src: 信子感觉到一种莫名其妙的羞耻感，

en: and silently took off the overcoat with its gorgeous lining and hung it in a corner of the entryway.
u.src: 她默默脱掉那件镶着华丽里子的大衣，挂在玄关的一角。

en: Shunkichi invited her into the eight-mat room that served as both study and sitting room and had her sit down,
u.src: 俊吉邀请她到书房兼客厅的八铺席房间坐下，

en: books were piled about the room in disorder,
u.src: 屋里散乱堆放着书籍，

en: especially around the red sandalwood desk beside the sunlit sliding partition,
u.src: 尤其是阳光照耀下的隔扇旁边的紫檀书桌周围，

en: newspapers, magazines, and manuscript paper were heaped there in such confusion that it dazzled the eye.
u.src: 凌乱堆满了报纸、杂志和稿纸，让人眼花缭乱。

en: the only thing in the room that suggested he shared his life with a young wife
u.src: 房中唯一能看出有年轻妻子共同生活的痕迹的，

en: was a single new koto set against the wall beside the alcove.
u.src: 只有放在壁龛旁边墙侧的一张新古琴。

en: For a little while, Nobuko looked over the whole room.
u.src: 有那么一会儿时间，信子打量了整个房间。

en: I saw the letter you wrote. I knew you would come sometime soon, but I did not expect it to be today.
u.src: “看到了你写的信。知道你最近会过来，只是没想到是今天。”

en: Shunkichi gazed kindly at Nobuko and lit a cigarette.
u.src: 俊吉亲切的望着信子，点燃了香烟。
“大阪的生活如何？”
“阿俊你过得如何？
幸福吗？”

en: Nobuko realized that after they had exchanged a few words, the old sense of familiarity and warmth had come back to life in her heart.
u.src: 信子察觉到，聊了几句之后，从前的熟悉和亲切感再次在她心理重生。

en: Although two years had passed and they had hardly written to each other, the awkward memory did not trouble her as much as she had imagined it would.
u.src: 虽然过去了两年的时间，他们也几乎没有写过信，但是这段尴尬的记忆并没有像想象中那么样让她觉得烦扰。

en: They sat around the brazier warming their hands and talked about many things,
u.src: 他们围坐在火盆旁边烤手，谈论很多话题，

en: including Shunkichi's fiction writing and friends they both knew,
u.src: 包括俊吉的小说创作，共同认识的朋友，

en: as well as the differences between Tokyo and Osaka, and it seemed there was no end to what they could talk about.
u.src: 还有东京和大阪的不同等等，似乎有聊不完的话。

en: But the two of them seemed to have agreed in advance,
u.src: 可是，他们两人好像商量好一样，

en: and did not mention anything at all about household expenses,
u.src: 完全不谈家庭开支方面的任何话题，

en: which made Nobuko feel deeply that she was talking with her cousin.
u.src: 这让信子深刻的干说道，她是在和表兄聊天。

en: But did they, too, have moments of silence?
u.src: 但是，他们是不是也会有沉默的时刻。

en: At that moment, Nobuko gazed at the brazier with a smile on her face.
u.src: 这时，信子就面带微笑的望着火盆。

en: Somewhere in her heart, she was faintly expecting something.
u.src: 她心理若有似无的期待着一些什么。

en: But whether deliberately or not, Shunkichi would always break the silence at just the right moment, find some topic they shared, and disturb her composure.
u.src: 但是，不知道是有意还是无意，俊吉总会适时打破沉默，找到共同话题，扰乱她的心绪。

en: Gradually, she could not help watching her cousin's expression, but he looked perfectly composed, with nothing unnatural about him.
u.src: 慢慢的，她不由不观察表兄的神情，不过他看起来神色自若，没什么不自然。

en: Before long, Teruko came back. When she saw her older sister, she excitedly clutched her hand and would not let go, while Nobuko was so moved that she laughed through tears.
u.src: 没过多久，照子回来了，看见姐姐，她兴奋的抓着姐姐的手不舍放开，信子激动的笑出眼泪来。

en: For a while, the two of them forgot Shunkichi was even there and eagerly asked each other about their lives since they had parted the previous year.
u.src: 一时间，两个人忘了俊吉的存在，你一言我一语的问对方去年分别以后的生活情况。

en: Teruko was glowing with energy, a flush on her face, and told her sister that she was still raising chickens.
u.src: 照子神采飞扬，脸上带着红晕，告诉姐姐她还在养鸡。

en: Shunkichi smoked as he watched the two excited sisters, smiling with deep satisfaction.
u.src: 俊吉抽着烟，望着激动的两个姐妹，心满意足的微笑。

en: Just then, the maid also came back and handed Shunkichi several postcards.
u.src: 这个时候，女佣也回来了，并递给俊吉几张明信片。

en: Shunkichi immediately sat down at the desk and began writing briskly.
u.src: 俊吉马上坐到书桌前，刷刷的开始了写作。

en: When Teruko realized that the maid had not been home earlier, she seemed a little surprised and said, "So when my sister came to the house, no one was home?"
u.src: 发现女佣之前并不在家，照子好像有些意外，说道：“所以，姐姐来家里的时候，没人在家吗？”
“当时只有阿俊在。”
信子故作镇定。

en: At that moment, Shunkichi turned his head toward Teruko and said, "I made the tea for you too, so you should be grateful to your husband."
u.src: 这个时候，俊吉扭过头来对照子说：“茶也是我替你沏的，你要感激你的丈夫。”

en: Teruko gave her sister a mischievous smile, but deliberately ignored her husband.
u.src: 照子恶作剧般对着姐姐笑了起来，却故意没搭理丈夫。

en: Before long, Nobuko, her younger sister, and her brother-in-law sat together around the dinner table.
u.src: 不多片刻，信子、妹妹、妹夫一同围坐在晚饭桌旁。

en: Teruko boasted to everyone that the eggs served at dinner had all been laid by chickens they kept at home.
u.src: 听照子跟大家炫耀，晚餐的鸡蛋都是家里养的鸡下的。

en: Shunkichi, as her brother-in-law, warmly urged Nobuko to drink some wine while talking in a socialist-sounding vein:
u.src: 俊吉作为妹夫一边热情的劝信子喝葡萄酒，一边谈一些社会主义核心价值观的论调：

en: People sustain their lives by plunder; if you look at it on the smallest scale, take these eggs we are eating, for instance...
u.src: “人们是靠掠夺维持生活的，从微小的地方来看，比如我们吃的这鸡蛋……”

en: But of the three of them, Shunkichi was undoubtedly the one who loved eggs the most.
u.src: 但是三个人当中，俊吉毋庸置疑是最爱吃鸡蛋的。

en: Teruko found this very funny and burst out laughing like a little child.
u.src: 照子觉得这很搞笑，像稚子般笑起来。

en: Moved by the atmosphere at the table, Nobuko could not help remembering the quiet dusk she had spent in the sitting room among the distant pines of Osaka.
u.src: 有感于饭桌上的气氛，信子情不自禁的想起来自己在遥远的大阪松林中的起居室里度过的寂静黄昏。

en: Even after they had finished the fruit served after dinner, there were still many topics left to talk about.
u.src: 吃完晚饭后的水果之后，还有很多话题没聊完。

en: Cousin Shunkichi, slightly tipsy after a little drink, sat cross-legged beneath the electric light of the long autumn night and began, with great enthusiasm, to show off his own peculiar Shunkichi-style sophistry.
u.src: 小酌后微醺的俊吉表兄盘膝而坐，漫漫长夜的电灯下，他开始兴致盎然的开始炫耀自己独特的俊吉式诡辩。

en: This spirited talk stirred in Nobuko memories of the youth she had gradually begun to forget, and she said, "Then I shall begin writing my novel too."
u.src: 这种意气风发的谈论，勾起了信子已经慢慢忘记的青春时光，说“那么我也开始我的小说创作吧。”

ja: らえることができるのだ」
en: Her cousin answered with a maxim from Nermont: "It is precisely because the Muses are women that men are able to capture them."
u.src: 表兄用内尔蒙的警言作答“正是因为缪斯们都是女人，因此，男人才能俘获她们。”

en: Nobuko and Teruko stood on the same side, opposing Nermont's authoritative pronouncement.
u.src: 信子和照子站在一条战线上，反对内尔蒙的权威论断。

ja: になるというのですか。
en: "If that is so, then does it mean that only women all become musicians?
u.src: “如果这么说的话，那么只有女人都当音乐家了吗？

en: But Apollo is a man, after all."
u.src: 但阿波罗就是男人啊。”
照子严肃的回答。

en: As night gradually grew late, Nobuko ended up staying at her younger sister's house.
u.src: 夜逐渐深了，信子终究住在了妹妹家。

en: Before going to bed, Shunkichi stepped out through one of the rain shutters on the veranda into the small garden.
u.src: 临睡之前，俊吉从檐廊上的一扇防雨门里走到了狭小的庭院中。

en: Then he called out, "The moon is lovely tonight; come out and look at it with me."
u.src: 接着，他招呼了一句：“今晚的月亮很不错，出来一起看啊。”

en: It was not clear whom he was calling to.
u.src: 也不知道是叫谁。

en: Nobuko walked alone behind Shunkichi and changed into garden clogs at the veranda.
u.src: 信子一个人走在俊吉身后，在檐廊处换上了庭院木屐。

en: Nobuko was barefoot, without tabi socks, and felt a slight chill.
u.src: 信子光着脚，没穿布袜，感到有些许清冷。

en: In the faint moonlight, her cousin stood under a withered cypress tree in one corner of the garden, looking up at the night sky.
u.src: 微微月光下，表兄站在庭院一隅的一颗干枯的扁柏树下，仰望夜空。

en: The grass grows so thickly here.
u.src: “这里的草生长的很茂盛啊。”

en: The desolate garden made Nobuko a little afraid,
u.src: 荒凉的庭院令信子有点害怕，

en: she cautiously drew closer to Shunkichi,
u.src: 她小心翼翼的靠近俊吉，

en: but Shunkichi kept looking up at the night sky and murmured, Today is the thirteenth day of the lunar month,
u.src: 可是俊吉依旧仰望夜空，低喃道：“今天是阴历十三呢，

en: so that is why the moon looks like this.
u.src: 怪不得月亮如此呢。”

en: After a brief silence, Shunkichi turned his head quietly and said to Nobuko, "Let's go look at them in the chicken coop."
u.src: 片刻沉默之后，俊吉默默的扭过头来，对信子说：“去鸡栏看看它们吧。”
信子点头默认。

en: The chicken coop stood opposite the cypress tree,
u.src: 鸡栏的位置在扁柏树对面，

en: and the two of them walked over there side by side.
u.src: 两人并肩前行，走到那边。

en: But inside the coop, apart from the smell given off by the chickens and faint traces of light and shadow, there was nothing else.
u.src: 不过，鸡栏里，除了鸡散发的气味和隐隐约约的光影，再无其他了。

en: Shunkichi looked at the chicken coop and murmured, "They've fallen asleep."
u.src: 俊吉看着鸡栏，喃喃自语：“它们睡着了。”

en: They were chickens whose eggs had been taken away by people...
u.src: “它们是被人们抢走了蛋的鸡……”

en: Nobuko could not help thinking that.
u.src: 信子不由得的这么想。

en: When the two of them came in from the garden, Teruko was gazing absent-mindedly at the electric lamp on her husband's desk.
u.src: 两人从庭院里进屋时，照子正望着丈夫书桌上的电灯出神。

en: A cicada like a green leaf was crawling over the lampshade.
u.src: 灯罩上有一只绿叶蝉在爬行。
